title: Determine whether a "Long tail" exists in a dataset
question:
I am working with a 200MB database that stores feedback from users about products in different years (Assume that 1 record = 1 feedback). The DB has the following schema

  • asin is a unique identifier of a product.

I am trying to determine if in any given year 20% of the products("asin") are accountable for more than 65% of the all feedbacks in that year ("Long-tail phenomena").

I tried to refer to the ASIN and the Year as a unique key and assign the value 1 to each time they key appeared. Then I would aggregate these values and would check if the first 20 ASIN count is bigger than 65% of all the feedback count. The following is an example of my code in PySpark:

reviews_rdd = reviews_df_split_date.rdd
print(type(reviews_rdd))

reviews_rdd\
.map(lambda r: ((r.asin, r.Year),1))\
.reduceByKey(lambda v1, v2: v1 + v2)\
.collect()

which produced the following output:

That's where I got stucked and didn't know how to group all ASIN in a given year and check the ASIN with the most feedbacks.

How can I check whether if less than 20% of the products in any given year account for over than 65% of all the feedbacks given in that year?
answer:
Aggregate feedback per ASIN per year. Calculate total feedback per year and percentage contribution per ASIN, cumulative feedback percentage, and Check if top 20% ASINs exceed 65% feedback:

from pyspark.sql.functions import col, count
feedback_counts = reviews_df_split_date.groupBy("Year", "asin").agg(count("*").alias("feedback_count"))

total_feedbacks_per_year = feedback_counts.groupBy("Year").agg({"feedback_count": "sum"}).withColumnRenamed("sum(feedback_count)", "total_feedbacks")

joined_df = feedback_counts.join(total_feedbacks_per_year, on="Year")

from pyspark.sql.functions import expr
joined_df = joined_df.withColumn("feedback_pct", col("feedback_count") / col("total_feedbacks"))

from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from pyspark.sql.functions import row_number
windowSpec = Window.partitionBy("Year").orderBy(col("feedback_count").desc())
ranked_df = joined_df.withColumn("rank", row_number().over(windowSpec))

from pyspark.sql.functions import sum as spark_sum
windowSpecCum = Window.partitionBy("Year").orderBy(col("feedback_count").desc()).rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)
ranked_df = ranked_df.withColumn("cum_feedback_pct", spark_sum("feedback_pct").over(windowSpecCum))

asin_counts = feedback_counts.groupBy("Year").agg(count("asin").alias("asin_count"))
ranked_df = ranked_df.join(asin_counts, on="Year")
ranked_df = ranked_df.withColumn("top_20_pct_threshold", col("asin_count") * 0.2)

result_df = ranked_df.filter(col("rank") <= col("top_20_pct_threshold"))\
    .groupBy("Year")\
    .agg(spark_sum("feedback_count").alias("top_feedbacks"),
         spark_sum("total_feedbacks").alias("total_feedbacks"))\
    .withColumn("top_pct", col("top_feedbacks") / col("total_feedbacks"))\
    .filter(col("top_pct") > 0.65)

This result_df will give you the years where the long-tail phenomenon is observed: less than 20% of products account for more than 65% of feedback.
